links.outcome: Reproducibility of chatbot responses across repeated queries two weeks apart (weighted kappa)
links.effect: Two-week reproducibility was fair for accuracy (weighted κ = 0.20) and completeness (κ = 0.29) and very low for safety (κ = 0.02, p = 0.81).
links.quote: Two-week reproducibility was fair for accuracy (weighted κ = 0.20, p = 0.009) and completeness (κ = 0.29, p = 0.001) and showed a very low κ in the safety scale (κ = 0.02, p = 0.81).

links.outcome: Chatbot advice accuracy against IDF-DAR guideline reference standard
links.effect: 77% fully consistent, 12% partially consistent, 11% (30/276) clinically harmful or contradictory advice.
links.quote: Overall, 77% of responses were fully consistent with the guideline, 12% were partially consistent, and 11% (30/276) contained clinically harmful or contradictory advice; harmful responses were about twice as common in Arabic as in English (14% vs. 8%).

screen.reason: Evaluates commercial LLM chatbots on standardized clinical scenarios regarding diabetes medication management during Ramadan without testing specific deployment safeguards.
